question: Can a chat model help users who have only unlabeled data and no seed prompt build a personalized prompt for a repetitive task?
hypothesis: A brief chat that surfaces data-aware output preferences and uses feedback on outputs yields a prompt whose zero-shot form matches its few-shot form.
contributions: CPE, a chat tool that builds a few-shot prompt from unlabeled user data and user feedback, with no labeled data or initial prompt
A three-party chat design (user, system, model) with context filtering, side-chats, CoT and API calls
A user study on summarization (12 sessions, 112 examples)

method.summary: CPE is a web chat in which Llama-3-70B analyses three user-provided unlabeled examples, asks data-aware preference questions, drafts an instruction, shows target-model outputs for the three examples, and revises the instruction and outputs from user feedback. The final deliverable is a few-shot prompt whose examples are the user-approved outputs. A user study compared a generic baseline prompt, the CPE zero-shot prompt and the CPE few-shot prompt on summarization.

eval.protocol: 12 participants each ran one chat then ranked summaries on a held-out unlabeled test split; ZS vs FS best-rate compared with a one-sample T-test (Drummond and Tom 2011); no significance reported for baseline vs CPE; no inter-annotator measure, one rater per session

prompts.text: Generate a concise and general prompt for a summarization task in one sentence.
Summarize the main points and key information from the provided text in a concise and clear manner, preserving the original meaning and content.

Analyze the conversation above, and share the comments made by the user on Examples 1-3. Any comment should be shared, even if minor. If no comment has been made, accept the prompt. If any comment has been made, recommend how to improve the prompt so it would produce the accepted outputs directly.

Before suggesting the prompt, briefly discuss the text examples with the user and ask them relevant questions regarding their output requirements and preferences. Please take into account the specific characteristics of the data. Your suggested prompt should reflect the user's expectations from the task output as expressed during the chat. Share the suggested prompt with the user before submitting it. Remember to communicate only via API calls.

limits: Only 12 sessions and one summarization user study; authors say limited annotators prevented evaluating other tasks.
Participants were researchers well-versed in prompt engineering, not typical users.
No comparison against automatic prompt optimisers (APE, OPRO, ProTeGi); no labeled-metric evaluation, deliberately.
Baseline is a single generic prompt, not a hand-written expert prompt.
Convergence is slow (25 min, 32 turns); authors defer improving it.
Target model, decoding settings and temperature not stated; no code or data released.
ZS vs FS test is a one-sample T-test; ZS~FS claim rests on non-significance (absence of evidence).
Open question whether CPE prompts improve as seeds for automatic prompt engineering.
